title: Caregiving and AI: research on family caregivers of adults and the AI that converses with them
include: Family members and friends who care, unpaid, for another adult.
AI that converses: chatbots, scripted ones included, and large language models, voice assistants and generative AI that answer or talk with people.

Studies in which those caregivers use, ask, judge or describe such AI, or in which it is built to support them, including surveys of how caregivers use it and studies of how it answers questions written as a caregiver would ask them.
Studies that compare how AI answers different people, when a caregiver, or someone asking for another adult, is one of them.
Research articles, preprints, reviews, benchmarks and datasets, and survey reports from named organisations, in English, published from 2023 on, and earlier work this area started from.
exclude: Parents caring for children, and paid care workers.
AI that does not converse, such as sensors, robots without a conversational part, and prediction models.
A language model used only as a research tool to analyse text about caregivers, such as their posts or interview transcripts.
Work that mentions caregivers only in passing, such as answers written for "patients and caregivers" that no caregiver took part in.
Editorials, commentaries, letters, news, vendor announcements, and conference abstracts with no paper.
